prompt: A scholarship goes to the top $10$ percent of scorers on an exam whose scores are approximately normal with mean $500$ and SD $100$. What is the minimum qualifying score? Round to the nearest whole number.
hint: This is a backward normal problem: you know the AREA (90 percent below the cutoff) and need the value.

hints.text: This is a backward normal problem: you know the AREA (90 percent below the cutoff) and need the value.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: the top $16$ percent starts at $z = 1$, so the cutoff would be $500 + 1(100) = 600$. Same move here, with the $z$ for the 90th percentile instead.
Find the $z$ with $0.90$ of the area to its left: $z \approx 1.28$ (invNorm$(0.90)$). Then unstandardize: $x = 500 + 1.28(100)$.
$x \approx 500 + 128 = 628$. A score of about $628$ is needed.

explanation: Top $10$ percent means $90$ percent of scores lie below the cutoff. In the standard normal table, an area of $0.90$ to the left corresponds to $z \approx 1.28$.
Turn that $z$-score back into an exam score with $x = \mu + z\sigma = 500 + 1.28(100) = 628$.
A student needs about $628$ to qualify. (A calculator gives $z = 1.2816$, so $628.2$, the same to the nearest point.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Reason from landmarks
steps: $z = 1$ is the 84th percentile (score 600) and $z = 2$ is the 97.7th percentile (score 700).
The 90th percentile must be between 600 and 700, and closer to 600.
628 fits that picture, so the table lookup is in the right place.

alternativeExplanations.title: The trap: looking up 0.10
steps: Searching the table for an area of $0.10$ gives $z = -1.28$, which is the BOTTOM 10 percent: a score of 372.
The scholarship wants the TOP 10 percent, which is the 90th percentile, $z = +1.28$.
Always sketch the curve and shade the region first: here the shaded tail is on the right.
